properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/24/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/24/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 960281
Permit API: 081-21878
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/24/2022
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. The north ditch line channel is estimated at 400 feet in length with spilled fluid flowing an additional 25-50 feet off the north and east corners of the pad (photos 4 and 8). During discussions with Mr. Hood, when the well switch over occurs, down well fluid volumes are reduced and the blender valves must be adjusted to correspond to the reduced flow rate. Mr Hood indicated that the spill was caused by the blender operator falling asleep and failing to close a valve connecting the blender pumps to the working tanks during the well switch. Prior to site departure, Andy Steffee, Project Manager with Creston Environmental, arrived on site with a crew to begin conducting site characterization and sampling activity. Based on unknown volume of fluid spilled, Mr.Barbier indicated that EQT will immediately begin Act 2 remediation work. Well stimulation activity is expected to last into August at this location. Violations noted during this inspection and outstanding violations are extended.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: HILCORP ENERGY CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/12/2024
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8208569
Permit API: 073-20398
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lawrence
Municipality: Pulaski Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/12/2024
Comments: Complaint (CTS #384838) received by Department on 10/25/2024. Operator (Hilcorp Energy Co) representative, Chris McCoy self-reported gas odor and possible leak of plugged OG well. The leak was discovered by the Operator while using a flare camera. Preliminary On-site Investigation performed on 10/29/2024. PA DEP representatives OGIS Rick Willey and OGI Thomas Antonishak met on location around 11 AM. No representation present from Operator. There are three active producing wells in addition to this plugged OG well in question on the well pad. All wells on pad are horizontal design and all target the Utica/Point Pleasant/Trenton formation(s). All active wells on pad are compliant with annual reporting of mechanical integrity and production. The cellar has been excavated and exposed around the Pulaski Kinkela 3H (073-20398) leaking plugged OG well. Virtual Meeting via Teams occurred on 10/31/2024 with the Department and Operator representatives to discuss further details about leaking plugged well, such as the prognosis and plan for re-entry/re-plug. Notice of Intention (NOI) to Plug well bore by Operator (Hilcorp Energy Co) of 073-20398 was received electronically via email on 11/07/2024. Department Authorization number issued and NOI officially received by OGI, Thomas Antonishak on 11/07/2024. NOI acknowledged, reviewed, signed, and submitted back to clerical by OGI, Thomas Antonishak on 11/12/2024. RePlugging operations planned to commence on 11/12/2024 with equipment mobilization and site access earthwork. The documents received by the Operator are attached to this inspection as Notice of Intention (NOI) (photo #1), Certificate of Plugging (photo #2), well record (photo #3), casing and cement record (photo #4), formation log (photo #5), and well location plat (photo #6) are included. The Certificate of Plugging and well record with casing/cement record files are attached to this inspection too. Location visited on 11/12/2024 in the morning to meet Operator representative Brian Reynolds, OGIS Rick Willey, and OGI Kyle Thomas. Additionally, a Production foreman from the Operator was present on site. Mobilization of equipment and material is occurring with anticipated rig up complete by tomorrow (i.e. 11/13/24) morning. There are three active, producing wells in addition to this plugged OG well in question on the well pad. The active wells include Pulaski Kinkela 4H (073-20384), Pulaski Kinkela 2H (073-20383), and Pulaski Kinkela 1H (073-20379). The well order and 5.5" casing pressures associated from a North to South direction: 4H with 300 psi, 3H with 0 psi, 2H with 240 psi, and 1H with 200 psi (photos #7, #8, #9, #10, and #11). There is pressure associated with each of the three active wells on pad. Altair multimeter gas detector utilized to take readings from each of the three active wells via various annular ports. The Altair meter did record methane and combustibles from all three adjacent, active wells annular ports. Steel plate monument was removed, gas bubbling was visible inside the 9 5/8" casing. Bubbling rate was steady and consistent (photos #12 and #13). OGI, Kyle Thomas and OGIS, Rick Willey witnessed occasional bubbles outside the 9 5/8" casing in the contained fluids within the cellar. Unable to determine where bubbles were coming from. Notice of Violation (NOV) issued for Plugging - General Provisions 78.91(a)- Failure to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore. The Operator self-reported leaking plugged OG well on 10/29/2024. Well was plugged on 09/14/2015 with Certificate of Plugging submitted and on record with the Department. Currently, rigging up manifolds, flow line tubular, and BOPs atop well-bore riser (photo #14). The rig and two frack tanks have arrived on site and are staged awaiting rig up (photo #15). Well posting signage at entrance to location, just before locked gate with all information about well and current Operator present (photo #16). Depart location.

Comments: On 4/24/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection at the Clara Jacques 1 well site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 4/20/2026. Inspection Date: 5/10/2024
Comments: On May 10, 2024, the Department conducted a FUI in Fayette County, Springfield Township on the MAWC 7020 Pad for a complaint received on April 11 2024 at 2:53. Accompanying in today's inspection was a MACW representative (Duane Goodsell) and Don Supcoe (Stone Ridge Energy). At the time of this inspection, the 1H and 3H wells were reported to be plugged with no monument present. The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road. The ERP and PPC Plan were onsite at the time of this inspection. The access road appears to stabilized with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. In the center of the pad near the location of reportedly plugged wells were previouslytwo stains that were oily in nature thatwere approximately 2ft by 2ft in size. The gravel has been removed from the two stained areas and the visually impacted materials placed into 5 gallon storage containers on-site. The Department recommended that the Operator remediate the areas as necessary in accordance with 78a66. It appears that the well site has yet to be restored. The Department recommends that the operator regrade, seed, and mulch site to obtain 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth and restore the well site. The completion of plugging for this well reportedly occurred 12/27/2023, therefore the Operator is in compliance with the COA issued on 12/16/2021. The Operator has 9 months from plugging to complete a restoration of the former well site. Discussion between MAWC and the Operator(Stone Ridge Energy) had taken place onsite about restoration efforts of the site during this inspection. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at this time. Violations are outstanding, but are listed as new in this inspection report due to an app error.

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all three wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21947, along with two other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21948, 019-21927), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2092885, 2092888, and 2092893 (conducted on August 17, 2012) suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections have indicated that the wells have been on inactive status since at least December of 2013. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0109 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 08/07/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. Up until very recently, the property owner had been grazing cattle on the site and using the tank pad as a feedlot. A small sediment slide had developed on the cut bank surface to the east of the well location. With the exception of the slide, there are currently no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site. Big Dog is currently preparing all of the wells on this site to be placed into production. A contractor hired by Big Dog was working on establishing new barbed wire fencing around the location when this inspection was conducted. Some production equipment, including 3 GPU's are being staged on the site. The slip on the cut surface above the location was discussed with the contractor. Containment under the GPU's was also discussed, as well as updated well tags.

A pump is placed and the operator is using it to pump water collecting in the berm into tanks on site. Water does not appear to have passed the berm at this time, at least superficially. Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 7/21/2025 at 0920 hours. The weather was 65 degrees F with cloudy skies.Remediation efforts are currently underway. A large pit has been excavated around the 7H well (photo #12) and the impacted material is piled onsite for later removal/disposal (photo #14). Repsol plans to have the wellhead reconstructed and then remedial efforts downslope will begin. The extent of downslope impacts off the western corner of the well pad and along the surface waterline in the adjacent field have been delineated. A temporary berm has been installed in the adjacent field, downslope of impacts, to collect fluids as runoff from precipitation occurs (photo #5). The surface waterline has been removed from the impacted area and from the constructed "corner" berm. Numerous areas of distressed vegetation were observed during this inspection (photos #2, 4, 8, 10 and 11).Resource Environmental (Resource), alongside Repsol's construction contractor, began screening and excavating impacted pad material and soils on Friday, 7/18/2025. Repsol reported that all material field measured at >1.0mS/cm is being recovered and stored for later disposal. Material recovered is being placed into lined residual waste containers which are then being covered prior to site departure. Repsol reported that three trucks are running today for removal of the residual waste containers as they are filled. Resource is screening material/soils every few feet, horizontally and vertically, to guide the excavation efforts.Repsol has Larson Design Group working on designing a more permanent type of land design downslope of the pad in order to continue the collection and recovery of fluids. Repsol plans to have a lined sump constructed within the temporary "corner" berm to continue collecting and recovering fluids. A "supervac" water truck is scheduled to arrive tomorrow morning to finish recovering all of the fluids held within the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) basin. The DEP recommends the following:-continuing fluids and impacted soils recovery-continuing monitoring nearby streams for potential impacts-continuing soil screening/monitoring to determine the extent of the impacts offsiteViolations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301The DEP departed the site at 1100 hours.

SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/05/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8248046
Permit API: 123-47821
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2025
Comments: The Loomis B Lease Loomis 7 OG well is the closest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the Loomis B lease. At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the Loomis 7 OG well. The Loomis B tank battery consists of two stock tanks, a produced fluids separator, and one subsurface produced fluids tank located inside earthen containment diking. The conventional wells on this lease were being produced at the time of this inspection. After arriving on the lease I began to inspect the condition of the tank battery. I found that the produced fluids separator and stock tanks in containment were equipped with PVC drain lines to separate any produced fluids that enter the tank battery from either the separator or the stock tanks into the subsurface produced fluids tank. At the time of this inspection, only the PVC drain line connected to the separator was found to be draining produced fluids. At the time of this inspection, the flowing PVC drain line was improperly positioned, as it was straddled on the edge of a cutout hole on the top of the subsurface produced fluids tank. The manner in which the drain line was situated allows the majority of the fluids flowing through the line to be released onto the top of the tank and ultimately onto the floor of the containment area, as opposed to inside the subsurface tank.The specific conductance of the accumulated fluid inside of the containment area measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. The soils below the fluid accumulating in the containment area also measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. A visual inspection of the containment area revealed additional signs of staining and stressed/dead vegetation around the produced fluids tank similar to that resulting from the ongoing release. This evidence is an indication of previous releases inside of the containment area prior to this inspection. At the time of this inspection, it did not appear that the pooling of fluids around the subsurface produced fluids tank were accumulating at a rate consistent with the volume of fluids being released into containment by the PVC drain. This and the evidence of stressed vegetation/oil staining around the proximity of the subsurface produced fluids tank referenced above suggests that the released fluids inside of the containment area are migrating into the soil below. A conservative estimate of a one gallon per minute discharge rate over the greater than 90 minute duration that I was present to observe the release suggests that more than 90 gallons (>2bbl) were released into the containment during this inspection.Sample number 4568-004 was collected from the fluid actively flowing from the PVC drain line and sample number 4568-005 was collected from the accumulated fluids inside of the containment area adjacent the subsurface produced fluids tank. These samples were sent to the DEP lab for SAC 942 analyses. After concluding my inspection, I called Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) at 14:59 and requested that he meet me immediately on the lease. Upon his arrival, I informed Kyle that I discovered a problem with the tank battery. I gestured to the ongoing release of fluids from the improperly placed PVC drain line. Kyle immediately placed the drain line into the cutout in the subsurface produced fluids tank. Kyle then phoned another TMP official to inform them of the release, but indicated that neither he or the other TMP official seemed to be aware of who had pumped the wells on this lease today. I informed Kyle that the release of fluids would be documented in this inspection report and that a Notice of Violations (NOV) would be included.A NOV is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8180320
Permit API: 117-21545
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/20/2024
Comments: A routine inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions. Six wells are staged for production on the well pad. The site surrounding the well pad was partially snow-covered during this inspection. A plugging rig is rigged up on the 2V well but was not in operation during this inspection. Multiple GPUs are present on the well pad. The GPUs appear to be in good condition. The well pad had many puddles of stormwater on it due to snow and rainfall earlier in the day. Most of the puddles of stormwater on the pad surface had an electrical conductivity (EC) of less than 1 mS/cm. Multiple puddles of fluid with an EC of greater than 19.99 mS/cm were observed covering an area on the pad surface approximately 25 ft by 15 ft just south of the 2V well head. I took sample 0718-232 from these puddles at 1405. The samples were sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Al, and Li.I spoke with Meagan DePue of Repsol by phone after my inspection on the same day at 1434. I informed her about the puddles which have an EC of greater than 19.99 mS/cm present on the pad surface. She said that she would have the puddles sucked up right away.The Department recommends vacuuming up the fluid from the pad surface. The Department recommends investigating the source of the fluid and excavating any impacted pad material. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of elevated EC fluid on the pad surface.Violations noted.

Comments: This inspection is being performed in response to a report of a previous spill that occurred in February. The API number was not observed on site.- The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site. The Department recommends that the Operator post their information on site in accordance with OGA 3211(G), until plugging operations are complete and the Certificate of Well Plugging (COWP) is approved by DEP Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.While on site, the Department spoke via phone with Operator representative Chris Caskey and informed them of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations in this inspection report. Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Springfield and Columbia Townships, Bradford County on 7/15/2025 at 1000 hours. The weather was around 80 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. A discussion with Repsol representatives indicated the following: The first plug on the 7H well was successfully set on 7/14/2025 at ~2100 hours. The flow of fluids from the well stopped after the first plug was set but "surging" was reported which was still causing fluids to reach the pad surface. A second plug was successfully set at ~0500 hours on 7/15/2025 which stopped all flow of fluids from the well. A third, precautionary plug was scheduled to be set on 7/15/2025. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed within the constructed "corner" berm (photo #4), the secondary berm/trench (photo #5), and the stormwater control basin (photos #7 and 8). The tertiary berm that was constructed as a precaution in the event of a rain event (photo #6) was observed to be dry today. The DEP continued creating/screening monitoring points around the pad, the stormwater control basin and downslope of the pad. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were noted downslope of the western corner of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm, which were also noted on 7/14/2025.The under-drain outlet pipe for the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) basin was plugged on 7/14/2025. Repsol observed that the plug was still dripping fluids so a secondary seal was placed over the outlet (photo #9).Resource Environmental (Resource) began evaluating potentially impacted areas onsite to determine the extent of the surface impacts of the release, including surface soils screening. Resource conducted drone flights to take high resolution overview photos of the site in order to produce a detailed map summarizing the screening points/data.As per the DEP recommendations on 7/14/2025, a wash station for cleaning of trucks prior to site departure was installed in the evening hours on 7/14/2025. The wash station can be seen in photo #1.As per 25 Pa. Code 78a.66b(4), Moody and Associates continued the sampling/screening of nearby water supplies on 7/15/2025.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301.The DEP recommends the following:-continuing the evaluation of impacted areas and executing a plan to prevent additional environmental impacts-covering impacted areas to prevent precipitation from saturating the soils-installing erosion and sediment control best management practices downslope of the exposed soil areas to prevent accelerated erosion/sedimentation from escaping the site-continuing fluid recovery The DEP departed the site at 1145 hours. For information regarding the DEP's inspection from 7/14/2025, please see inspection record #4012602.

At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to a fresh water impoundment located on site. The graveled well pad in this incident appeared to be scraped, the ground in this area was observed to be brown and muddy in comparison to the dry and gray graveled well pad surrounding this area. Ms. Karosic stated that 2-4 inches of the well pad in this incident area was scraped and vacuums were used to suck up any puddles of fluid. The secondary containment where this incident occurred appeared to be clean and dry.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed 3 clamshell dumpsters on site, 2 were full of contaminated material and the 3rd will be filled with any remaining contaminated material once Moody arrives to conduct further remediation efforts.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected readings of 8.30 mS, 3.07 mS and 2.20 mS in the incident area and 8.21 mS underneath/at the base of the clean water impoundment. The area outside of this incident area where the ground was not scraped was also screened and the readings collected in that area was comparable to the background reading of 0.333 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign. At the time of this inspection, the DEP notified Ms. Karosic of the elevated soil conductivity readings in the incident area and underneath the fresh water impoundment. Ms. Karosic stated that fracking operations is scheduled to commence between July 10-11, 2025, then the fresh water impoundment will be removed and remediation can be conducted in the area where the impoundment was located. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that at this time they estimate that the quantity of the release is between 1 and 3 barrels and that they anticipate following Act 2 protocol for the clean up. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed SDSs for all chemicals on site and included in the release mixture to be located in the on site trailer. Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the 1-3 barrel release of produced water, fresh water, and fracking chemicals on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

Violation ID: 990003
Permit API: 015-23753
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/30/2023
Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 25 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested some of these with an Oakton PCTS 50 for conductivity and discovered a 60' x 60' ice/water puddle southeast of the wellheads and adjacent to the south edge of the secondary containment for six frac tanks that field tested at 4.05 mS conductance. Sample 9551-049 was collected from this puddle. Two water puddles between the two frac tank secondary containments field tested at 1.5 mS conductance. Other water puddles tested at less than 0.6 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance fluids with Chesapeake's Kyle Stephens. He directed an arriving vac truck to start sucking up the fluids. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization has been applied to the perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place down slope from the infiltration areas.There were five wells staged for flowback/production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks in secondary containment that were connected to the wellheads. There were 10 frac tanks on the north side of location that were stationed in secondary containment but were not connected to the well heads at the time of the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface while cleaning up after fracking operations were completed and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.The release of a large volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402[b)The DEP recommends the following:1. Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.2. Continue to monitor the areas with temporary stabilization and apply addition resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 1010 hours.

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: On March 16, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline and Brooke Millisock conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The DEP observed and sampled five seeps and four stream sites that were found off the west side of the well pad in "Deep Hollow" along an UNT to Rattlesnake Run. STL Resources revealed that the seeps were occurring and being monitored for specific conductivity and chlorides on March 1, 2022 during a meeting with the DEP. The data that STL Resources provided showed levels of elevated conductivity in seeps 1, 1A, and 4. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling site for pH and conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 had a pH of 8.61 and conductivity of 29.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The DEP observed and sampled five seeps and four stream sites that were found off the west side of the well pad in "Deep Hollow" along an UNT to Rattlesnake Run. STL Resources revealed that the seeps were occurring and being monitored for specific conductivity and chlorides on March 1, 2022 during a meeting with the DEP. The data that STL Resources provided showed levels of elevated conductivity in seeps 1, 1A, and 4. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling site for pH and conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 had a pH of 8.61 and conductivity of 29.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: On 10/11/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Blacksville I BIP32 Well in Wayne Township, Greene County in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug a well The NOI was received by The Department on 9/9/2024 and 10/1/2024 due to plugging schedule changes.On site at the time of inspection were contractors associated with well plugging. The contractors indicated that the plugging rig was set up on 10/8/2024, and they expected the plugging operation to take 3 days to complete.While on site I observed the following:-The access road appeared to be in generally good condition. I recommend that the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) installed along the access road receive additional aggregate if contractors expect to be on site for additional time (Photos 1-6).-I observed a silt fence filled with sediment at STA 14+00. I observed sediment that bypassed the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entered a stream identified by E and S plans as UNT to Dunkard Creek. Scouring left of the culvert outlet was evident where sediment bypassed the silt fence. Sediment accumulation was evident throughout the streambed and significant sediment buildup was present within the culvert outlet. I followed sediment within the streambed for approximately 50 feet below the culvert outlet (Photos 7-15).-I observed no sediment accumulation above the timber matting crossing at the culvert inlet, indicating that sediment entered the stream where it bypassed the perimeter silt fence (Photo 16).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 15+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 17).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 18+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 18).-The plugging rig was installed at the time of inspection. All equipment was staged on the plugging pad. I was unable to see if secondary containment was installed at the plugging rig due to equipment being staged close to the rig (Photos 21-22).-The plugging pad perimeter was lined with reinforced silt fence, which appeared to be functioning properly. I observed no signs of accelerated erosion around the plugging pad (Photos 23-24).Due to sediment bypassing the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entering UNT to Dunkard Creek, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, 78.53, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/21/2021 to SWN PROD CO LLC in Stevens Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/21/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 934592
Permit API: 015-22245
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Stevens Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/21/2021
Comments: On 10/21/2021, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Greenzweig (U Pad). This inspection is to evaluate the site after an engine oil spill was reported to the department on 10/20/2021. When I arrived on site I met two SWN personnel, Mike Deming and Seth Tratthen. Also on site were two men from Resource Environmental Management Inc. I have contact info for John Salinkas. Description of event: A compressor station is in the process of being removed from the site. A crew from a third party company, Pilot Thomas, was removing fluids from the equipment prior to the equipment being loaded on trucks. Unused engine oil was being transferred from a 500-gallon tank to a 300-gallon tote that was already on a truck. The tote did not have a cap on the two inch drain valve and the tote was strapped down on the truck with the drain valve not immediately accessible by the crew. As the crew was pumping into the tote, they suspected something was wrong with the pumping process. They checked the progress and found the drain valve partially open and leaking fluids onto the ground. They stopped pumping and had to unstrap the tote before manhandling it to a position where they could reach and close the valve. It is estimated that 120 gallons of HDAX 5200 Low Ash Gas Engine OIl was released onto the unprotected ground. This was next to edge of the pad. A perimeter berm kept the fluid from flowing off property and down the fill slope. Response: A truck on site that could pick up fluids was used to collect 90 gallons of free liquid. A skid-steer was brought to location and excavated a 40' long x10' wide x2.5' (maximum measurements) trench. The excavated material was loaded into two 30yd rolloff dumpsters. While I was still on site, both dumpsters were loaded onto trucks and hauled away to an industrial landfill. I was shown the excavated area where the spill had impacted. I did not witness any signs of free liquid or additional contamination. I was told that the cleanup crew tested the excavation area to determine if clear of contamination before ending excavation. No E&S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appears stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. There are a total of 3 wells staged for production. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. The well cellars are filled with gravel. All GPUs and production tanks were stationed in secondary containment. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations 78a 56(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b) The department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c).

Comments: On May 18, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4179991.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/20/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 12/20/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plan is on site.- Disturbance along the access road entrance appears to have been regraded at this time (Photos 1-3).- The length of the access road and the well site also appear to have been regraded at this time, including the earthen berm along the access road. - No seed and/or mulch is observed on the regraded access road and site at this time. - The production tank and equipment near and within the earthen berm appear to have been removed from the site (Photo 7). - CFS at the inlet and outlet of the culvert that runs under the access road does not appear to be implemented/maintained properly at this time. - The CFS at the outlet side appears to be overtopping causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation which is observed on the other side of the CFS (Photos 10-13).- Some of the sedimentation observed further downslope in the previous inspection is not visible at this time due to vegetation that appears to have grown on top (Photo 14).- CFS on site does not appear to be implemented/maintained properly at this time (Photos 15-18). The Department recommends the operator chink the CFS.- A section of the slope below the well site is observed to have no CFS below (Photos 19-20). Sediment at the bottom of this section of the slope appears to have been graded/pushed on to piles of brush (Photos 22-25). The Department recommends installing additional CFS where necessary, per the E and S plans. - Well appears to be plugged and buried at this time. Violations remain outstanding for failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, and failure to implement and maintain E and S BMPs.

Comments: On September 15 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the E Shuster 2 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid.At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking and/or overflowed, but did not appear to be actively leaking. The tank appeared to be approximately 80% full at the time of the inspection.At the base of the production tank, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. There appeared to be absorbent mats on the ground next to and under the production tank where the release appeared to have occurred. Based on the amount of fluid on the ground observed by the Department, this appeared to be a reportable release (5 gallons or more). A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.05mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. While some readings appeared comparable to the background reading, others were elevated in comparison to the background reading. Readings of 0.09mS 0.10mS, 0.14mS 0.31mS, 0.39mS, 0.41mS, 0.49ms, 0.64mS, 1.39mS, 1.33mS were obtained by the Department. Elevated readings were detected in about a 1 foot radius around the production tank.Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted operator representative Joe Miller to inform him of the release. Mr. Miller indicated that they had replaced/repaired a faulty dump valve the week prior. He stated field members would be at the site to assess the area for a release and remediation would occur as necessary. The Department recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 7 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include:1.) An incident report including the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined.2.) How long it is believed the release was occurring,3.) A timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.4.) Clarification/waste manifests for any production fluid or other production waste that has been disposed of from the site in the last 2 years.The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

Comments: OGI's Eric Miller and Todd Martin were on site today to witness the ending of the 72 hr. PBUT (Pressure Build Up Test). This test was performed to evaluate the recent remedial work completed by the Operator. The current WBS (Well Bore Schematic) is included in the files and pictures sections of this report. Upon arrival the wells annuli were shut in. Creston Environmental reps. The Department recommends the removal of wellhead, above the A section flange to allow unrestricted venting of any residual gas prior to moving forward with the final cement plug placement. The Dept. would like to recheck this well ~ 30 days after the unrestricted venting has been established. Please contact OGIS Ken Kennedy (kenkennedy@pa.gov) when this can be arranged.

Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. What appear to be third-party vehicle tracks were observed at the former well pad location (photo 7). The Department recommends that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site.The super silt fence remains installed at the northern boundary of the former well site (photos 12 and 13). The operator reports that it pre-exists well site construction. The operator provided photos of the silt fence via email that were reportedly taken on 1/29/2026, and stated that the vegetative growth shown in the photos through the super silt fence could not have occurred since September of 2025; when the operator reportedly started site reclamation.No loose sediment was observed in the channel that empties into the Sediment Trap that reportedly pre-exists well site construction (photos 16 and 19).The Department recommends continued mulching and seeding of the former well site to establish adequate vegetative growth in the forthcoming spring.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.
